Philippine Overseas Employment Administration PRE-EMPLOYMENT ORIENTATION SEMINAR (PEOS ONLINE) MODULE 1: PRICEST

What factors should I consider before deciding to work overseas?

Let's take a closer look at the concerns you are faced with when you work abroad.

For your easy reference, the catchword is: "PRICEST"

P - Physical Mobility R- Relationships I- Income & Expenses C - Career Movement & Direction E - Environment S - Skill Set T - Time

"PRICEST" : Physical Mobility

Your ability to move around as you are used to will be limited when you are in the country of your destination.

You may be stationed in a compound with other workers or in a 5 x 10 square meter condominium apartment.

You may be stationed in a compound with other workers or in a 5 x 10 square meter condominium apartment.

It's going to be mostly doing the tasks assigned you, and not much movement - and free time - as you please.

"PRICEST" : Relationships

When you work abroad, you will be leaving your spouse or partner, your children, your parents, friends, and co-employees behind.

You won't be around when birthday or anniversaries are celebrated, or someone close to you is sick or needs your presence.

This can be very stressful. Be ready to cope.

"PRICEST" : Income and Expenses

Chances are you will be earning more with your job abroad compared to your salary in the Philippines, but remember expenses also increase proportionately.

Your family may require more financial help from you, aside from paying the personal loans and advances you incurred when you were preparing your trip.

You need to balance income with your expenses.

"PRICEST" : Career Movement and Direction

As you are hired for a specific job abroad, you should not expect a promotion to the next higher position in your next posting.

Your assignment to a particular position will most likely remain the same for the entire duration of your employment contract.

Furthermore, the renewal of your contract is solely dependent on your employer.

"PRICEST" : Environment

Furthermore, the renewal of your contract is solely dependent on your employer.

"PRICEST" : Environment

More than the different physical environment - different climate and seasons - of an overseas posting, you will need to adjust to a new culture altogether:

Language so unfamiliar, prescribed type of clothing, different and limited food choices or even taste of food you are not accustomed to, places inaccessible to you, and social relations.

"PRICEST" : Skill Set

A number of job openings may interest you - be sure your qualifications as to education and experience (skill set) match with requirements of the job.

If you need to brush up on your know-how and level of experience before signing the employment contract, do so.

Go, when you're truly ready!

"PRICEST" : Time

If you need to brush up on your know-how and level of experience before signing the employment contract, do so.

Go, when you're truly ready!

"PRICEST" : Time

Working abroad means someone else - your employer - specifies the length of time you should accomplish a task.

It is in this sense that "time is not in your hands." But that is one discipline we can all benefit from; our individual productivity increases with the proper use of time!

PARDA- Important Issues

Alongside "PRICEST" you have to personally confront 5 very important issues -

P - Preparedness to temporarily leave your family behind A - Appropriate qualifications to fill in the position you are applying for R - Readiness to work in an unfamiliar, foreign environment D - Determination to face new challenges and risks A - Availability of money to spend for the job application

Adopting a positive disposition regarding these will certainly pave the way for a clearer and less bumpy road ahead!

MODULE 2: JOB SEARCH

Your Job Search

There is no substitute for doing it right the first time! Your search for a job overseas must begin in the right, legal way. This means dealing only with duly authorized recruitment agencies.

The Philippine Overseas Employment Administration (POEA) issues licenses to these agencies to recruit and employ Filipino overseas. Their participation in the country's overseas employment program is crucial: they take charge of the recruitment, hiring, and deployment of our countrymen as well as ensure the strict implementation of employment contracts.
The POEA does not encourage direct hiring or name hiring as employers have no local representatives to answer for any toward incident.

Your Job Search: The Recruitment Agency

To make sure you're dealing with a duly licensed recruitment agency, simply log on to www.poea.gov.ph

This is the POEA official website. Check the recruitment agency's name in the list of licensed companies. Make sure it also has an approved job order for the position you are applying for.

A company not included in the POEA list is an illegal recruiter.

DO NOT DEAL WITH IT!

A company not included in the POEA list is an illegal recruiter.

DO NOT DEAL WITH IT!

When applying through a recruitment agency, have the following documents ready: 1. Birth Certificate issued by the National Statistics Office (NSO)For married women, obtain an NSO copy of your marriage contract 2. Muslim applicants need a certification from the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos 3. Transcript of School Records and Diploma authenticated by the Department of Education or Commission on Higher Education 4. Training Certificates from TESDA or training institute or company 5. These documents will be processed by the agency and submitted to the employer.

When you receive the good news that the employer has selected you, proceed to do the following: 1. Read and study carefully the Employment Contract presented to you. If you agree to all the provisions, sign it. 2. Undergo medical examination in a DOH-accredited clinic; submit the result to agency. 3. Attend the Pre-Departure Orientation Seminar (PDOS) in an OWWA-accredited 4. PDOS provider and get your Certificate of Attendance; submit this to the agency.

Note: It is at this point that the agency will submit all your documents to the POEA for processing. The POEA will then issue an e-Receipt also known as the Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC).

Your Job Search: Government Placement Branch (GPB)

Your Job Search: Government Placement Branch (GPB)

You may also check out POEA's Government Placement Branch (GPB). Governments of other countries deal directly with the POEA to recruit workers from the Philippines.

These countries have their respective recruitment programs.

For example: South Korea - Employment Permit System Japan - PJEPA Germany - Triple Win

The GPB also recruits nurses and other medical health workers for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia-Ministry of Health.

Applicants for the GPB job openings must register online through the POEA's website and the Manpower Registry Division.

The following documents must also be ready: 1. NSO issued Birth Certificate 2. NSO issued marriage contract 3. National Commission on Muslim Filipinos certification for 4. Muslims 5. DepEd or CHED Transcript of Records or Diploma 6. TESDA or training center certificate 7. Two (2) pieces passport size or 2"x2" pictures 8. Six (6) pieces passport size or 2"x2" pictures for Ministry 9. of Health- KSA applicants 10. Certificates of Employment of at least two (2) years' 11. experience in one position 12. Passport (for applicants with overseas job experience)

IF APPLICABLE: 1. License/Board 2. Valid Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) 3. Identification Card 4. Board License 5. Board Rating 6. Post graduate diploma

Thereafter, have your medical examination in a DOH accredited clinic as well as do the following:

Attend the Pre-Departure Orientation Seminar (PDOS) conducted by OWWA at the POEA building and get your Certificate of Attendance; submit the medical result and PDOS Certificate of Attendance to GPB.

Obtain your e-Receipt/Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC)

Your Job Search: Name/Direct Hiring

Browsing through the web, periodicals, and/or referrals from relatives and friends may give you a job lead overseas.

This is what is commonly referred to as NAME-HIRING or DIRECT HIRING. A Name-Hire applicant is one seeks employment on his own without the participation of a third party, or a recruitment agency. Tread cautiously!

Great care must be exercised when considering this option. Applicants are strongly advised to coordinate directly with the POEA's Name Hire Processing Unit. A personal visit to Unit will be greatly advantageous to you.

Your prospective employer will prepare an Employment Contract in your name and submit it to the nearest Philippine embassy for authentication and verification. The employer will take charge of your visa and work permit in the host country, send you a round-trip airline ticket, and money for processing fees.

Your Job Search: Government Placement Branch (GPB)

Your Job Search: Government Placement Branch (GPB)

Prepare the following documents: 1. NSO issued Birth Certificate 2. NSO issued marriage contract 3. National Commission on Muslim Filipinos certification for Muslims 4. DepEd or CHED Transcript of Records or Diploma 5. TESDA or training center certificate

You need to do the following, too:

1. Undergo your medical examination at an accredited DOH clinic, if required;obtain a copy of your Medical Certificate. 2. Attend PDOS conducted by OWWA at the POEA and obtain the Certificate of Attendance; 3. Submit your Employment Contract/Offer of Employment, employment visa/work permit, together with the medical and PDOS certificates at the Name Hire Processing Center, 2nd Floor, Blas F. Ople Building, Ortigas Ave., cor EDSA, Mandaluyong City.

Your Job Search: The Overseas Employment Certificate

Here's a very important footnote about the Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC). 1. The OEC is proof that your documents have been processed at the POEA, including payments for POEA processing fee, OWWA, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions. 2. Remember, only documented workers are entitled to the full protection of the law as well as the benefits of the programs and services of the government. Your OEC has a 2-month validity from the date of issuance; this means the agency should deploy you within this period. 3. Your OEC is your travel exit clearance at the airport when you leave. You are exempted from paying the travel tax and terminal fee!

MODULE 3: FOREWARNED, FOREARMED

FOREWARNED, FOREARMED: Stay away from Illegal Recruiters!

There will always be people who will try to lure you into what would appear to be an easier way to get a job abroad.

Be very careful! Stay away from them!

A person, company or entity without a license or authority from the POEA who

C - Canvass E - Enlist, T- Transport C- Contract, H- Hire U - Utilize P - Procure workers for employment abroad whether for profit or otherwise is an illegal recruiter.

It also includes the following:

C - contract services R - referring P - promising A- Advertising for employment abroad.

Be a documented OFW!

It also includes the following:

C - contract services R - referring P - promising A- Advertising for employment abroad.

Be a documented OFW!

As your future - as well as your loved ones - is at stake, you need to be vigilant at all times. You must exert due diligence every step of the way. Do not be misled or influenced by mere hearsay; be critical of what you read. Seek confirmation from the POEA itself. Here are some pointers for you to seriously take into account -

Deal only with licensed recruitment agencies; they are the only ones authorized to recruit and deploy workers.

An agency without a license means it is an illegal recruiter!

How you can be safe from illegal recruiters:

1. Make sure the licensed agency has a POEA approved job order.

2. Deal only with authorized representatives of a licensed agency; an ID is not enough. Licensed agencies are required to post their organizational charts as well as the names and photos of their officers and employees. 3. Transact business only in the registered office address of the licensed agency; be sure the publicized office and the office you are going to are one and the same. 4. Pay only the maximum allowable placement fee of one month of the basic salary, exclusive of documentation cost. But collection of such fees from seafarers and household service workers (HSWs) are prohibited. There are countries like the United Kingdom, Ireland, Norway, the Netherlands, and the provinces of Canada: Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia that do not allow collection of

There are countries like the United Kingdom, Ireland, Norway, the Netherlands, and the provinces of Canada: Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia that do not allow collection of placement fees. 5. Pay the placement fee after signing the Employment Contract; demand an official receipt (OR) 6. Do not send money by money transfer or remittance of any form just to receive application forms or to process your papers in exchange of a job abroad. 7. When offered a tourist or visit visa to work abroad, turn it down. A legal job offer means a visa or work permit will be issued you. 8. Deal directly with government offices; avoid fixers! 9. Memorize : www.poea.gov.ph

Illegal Recruiters Think They're Clever, But you know Better!

Know the modus operandi of illegal recruiters. Here are some of the tactics they use to mislead and extract hard-earned money from job applicants.

Blind Advertisements - Without completely identifying themselves, recruiters advertise job openings in newspapers asking applicants to send in their papers via a P.O. Box address, and a minimal processing fee. You will never know for a fact what they advertise is for real. There is no way you can check this! Chances are they will continue to ask more money to continue with the "processing" of your papers!

Correspondence - Like the blind advertisements, you are asked to submit your job application through the mail together with a minimal processing fee. Don't be misled!

Correspondence - Like the blind advertisements, you are asked to submit your job application through the mail together with a minimal processing fee. Don't be misled!

Tourist Visa, Worker Talaga ! - Illegally recruited workers leave the country as tourists to work abroad. Without proper documentation, workers who fall for this trap are open to abuse and cannot report cases of maltreatment because they are working illegally. Worst of all, you cannot enforce the contract in court. Do things right! Go through the legal process the POEA provides and enjoy enormous benefits you are entitled to.

Escort Services

- Unscrupulous persons escort workers to the airports and stealthily board the plane without the required travel documents. When they can no longer back out, the workers will be forced to pay hundreds of thousands of pesos as facilitation fee.

Backdoor Exit - Illegally recruited workers leave the country through the southern ports of exit where immigration control may be lax. They board cargo ships or boats. Once abroad they are on their own - no one to protect them from employers' abuses, no benefits to enjoy.

Forged Documents - Illegal recruiters facilitate the departure of workers from the Philippines using falsified documents, i.e., birth certificate, "baklas" passports; - illegal recruiters use this to deploy minors.

Direct Hire - In this type of illegal activity, an employer hires Filipino job applicants without going through POEA or Philippine licensed agencies. The law prohibits direct hiring.

Trainee-Worker Scheme - Under the pretext that they are going to be trained abroad, applicants are asked to sign a Training Agreement with the recruiter but actually works in hotels/restaurants in a foreign country where they are just given allowances or paid salaries way below those given regular employees

Tie-up of Kabit System (Repro-scheme) - Unlicensed agencies recruit workers using the facilities of a licensed recruiter : a worker is processed using the job order of a licensed agency. Upon reaching the country of destination, the actual job given is not the actual job stated in the job order. For example the papers of a household worker is processed as nurse, saleslady or janitress.

Visa Assistance or Immigration Consultancy - There are some companies that operate as consultants to guide applicants on how to obtain an immigrant visa; this is legal. But offering a job overseas is illegal. Always be on guard!

Seminars/Sports Events/Conferences - Illegal recruiters facilitate the participation of applicants to well-known seminars, sports events or conferences abroad, then stay to work there.

Mail Order Bride Scheme - Recruiters arrange the marriage between Filipino women and foreigners. Once in the country of destination, the "wife" ends up as a domestic helper and suffers immeasurably!

Online Scam - Spam and scam rhyme - be very careful when receiving notices of job availabilities abroad! Do not give information freely about yourself or other data that scammers may use to develop a very tempting job offer.

- The bottom line is to immediately check and confirm with the POEA. Remember, an agency without a POEA license is an illegal recruiter without a conscience! - Do not fall for offers for an easier way to go abroad. As a completely documented worker, you are entitled to the government's full protection! Enjoy your rights, privileges, and benefits! The POEA way is definitely the right way!

By Correspon dence - Interested applicants are encouraged to submit the requirements for application through mail together with a seemingly minimal fee.

By Correspon dence - Interested applicants are encouraged to submit the requirements for application through mail together with a seemingly minimal fee.

Educational Tours - Victims recruited will travel in a group of two or more as students. The recruiter will prepare the documents to be presented at the airport that include school credentials to prove that they are students.

Religious Pilgrimage - Usually traveling as a group and presenting credentials of their religious affiliations supposedly to go for a pilgrimage but with the end purpose of working upon reaching their destination.

Detached Visa - Worker intending to work in South Korea under E-6.2 Visa (Entertainer Visa issued by Korean Embassy) misrepresents by travelling either as a tourist or worker to the Middle East but with connecting flight to an Asian country. The visa is detached from the passport for purposes of departing from the Philippines but attaches the same visa upon reaching transit, and boards onward flight to Korea, circumventing the POEA requirements for OFW in destination country

NAIA Terminal 3 Open Market - Recruiters at NAIA Terminal 3 are waiting for off-loaded passengers and offering them immediate deployment bragging about their connections with Immigration Officers.

NAIA Terminal 3 Open Market - Recruiters at NAIA Terminal 3 are waiting for off-loaded passengers and offering them immediate deployment bragging about their connections with Immigration Officers.

Wedding/ Grand Occasion Invitation - Passengers traveling to attend a fictitious ceremony, carrying complete apparel and formal printed invitation.

" Syota " System - Two persons, a male and a female, having no relation with each other, pose as lovers and tourists on a leisure trip but they will separate upon reaching their destination. They

will go to their final destination. Only one of them will return to the Philippines but there is a possibility that both of them would not.

"Yaya”' Method - A minor child who will travel to see her parent abroad is accompanied by her "yaya". The yaya possesses necessary documents induding the required clearance signed by the parent. Afterwards, the child will return to the Philippines accompanied by her parent and the yaya left behind

Internet Scam - Advertisement and recruitment of workers for overseas employment through the internet which are meant to defraud, traffic or smuggle workers. Various internet users have complained of having been victimized by bogus websites that require applicants to immediately remit money through money transfer services for intended visa, airfare and processing fees. - Sending appointment letters to applicant workers and asking them to send money to travel agencies to arrange their travel requirements. - Use of mobile phone or email as a means to contact the alleged employer/agent (scammer) without giving any landline number, or if there is one, it cannot be contacted. - Designation of unauthorized third parties or agents, and in some cases alleged immigration officers, to process their

without giving any landline number, or if there is one, it cannot be contacted. - Designation of unauthorized third parties or agents, and in some cases alleged immigration officers, to process their work permit applications and visas. - Use of scanned recruitment documents such as special power of attomey, recruitment agreement, manpower request, and business or registration papers. - Giving fake websites that purportedly contain employer's information and other details which are expectedly incorrect.

Beware: Your recruiter maybe a drug trafficker!

The emerging trend in transporting illegal drugs using "drug couriers" has become a worldwide concern because it poses serious threats to health, it violates human rights and it cultivates illegal activities and other crimes such as trafficking and prostitution.

Human traffickers and illegal recruiters have joined forces with drug traffickers to target prospective OPWs especially those heading for Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states that have a "no tourist visa" pact with the Philippines.

These unsuspecting OFWs are being used as drug couriers, often decelved by their recruiters about their real jobs or the conditions of their employment overseas.

These unsuspecting OFWs are being used as drug couriers, often decelved by their recruiters about their real jobs or the conditions of their employment overseas.

Modus Operandi of Drug Traffickers ● Couriers are usually recruited by casual acquaintances they meet in the Philippines or abroad, mostly fellow Filipinos connected to drug syndicates like the African Drug Syndicate (ADS), offering plane tickets, hotel accommodation and huge amounts of money.

● Members of syndicates befriend/marry potential recruit then later turn him/her into a courier or cohort. ● Opium Poppy . Courters may also be recruited through the internet and social networking sites like Facebook, MySpace Tagged, etc. ● Drug traffickers can also turn their recruits into seasoned drug mules by having them repeatedly carry drugs in exchange for a big amount of money. ● Drug traffickers pose as recruiters offering jobs mostly in non.visa countries such as in ASEAN member states - Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Brunel, and Thailand, but later duped them into canying packages, not knowing that drugs were placed inside. ● Drug traffickers who pose as recruiters also lend their bags to the results or request recruits to bring a package as "pasalubong" for someone.

● Unwitting victims are duped by acquaintances into carrying packages in exchange for money, not knowing that the package has illegal drugs or substances placed inside. ● Syndicates also engage in travel & tours businesses/ agencies to arrange airline and hotel bookings of the couriers and use fraudulent documents/take credit cards.

How to Avoid Being a Drug Courier ● Make sure that you are dealing with a licensed recruiter, and that you have a contract with a definite employer. ● Even if certain countries do not require visas for tourists, a work visa or permit is still required in order to work in these countries. ● Be vigilant on people offering easy money and work abroad especially when you are unsure of the nature of the job. ● Avoid bringing other people's luggage/packages especially when you do not know what is contained inside. Do not trust anybody, even acquaintances, when you are traveling abroad. A big amount of money is not worth it.

Illegal Recruiters Think They're Clever, But you know Better!

Illegal Recruiters Think They're Clever, But you know Better!

The bottom line is to immediately check and confirm any job offer with the POEA. Remember, an agency without a POEA license is an illegal recruiter without a conscience!

Do not fall for offers promising an easier way to go abroad. As a documented worker, you are entitled to the government's full protection. Enjoy your rights, privileges, and benefits.

Should you encounter an illegal recruiter, report him or her to POEA. Go to our Operations and Surveillance Division at the 4th floor, Blas F. Ople Bldg., Mandaluyong City

The POEA way is definitely the right way!

MODULE 4: GET THE PRICES RIGHT

Get The Prices Right

As the saying goes, "there are no free lunches." There's a price to pay for future benefits you will be enjoying when you work abroad. It is prudent to know which fees you have to pay and which ones are to be paid by your employer or recruitment agency.

1. Placement Fee ● The maximum allowable placement fee you will have to pay the recruitment agency is equivalent to your one-month basic salary. ● Pay this only after you have signed the contract; demand an Official Receipt (OR) in exchange for your payment. The OR must show the actual amount paid and purpose/s for such payment. Remember: seafarers and household service workers (HSW) need not pay placement fees. ● Take note there are countries that prohibit the collection of placement fees from workers : the United Kingdom, Ireland, Norway, the Netherlands, and the Canadian provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia. ● You will also have to shoulder the following: ○ PhilHealth Insurance Premium - Php2,400.00 (Valid for 1 Year) ○ Pag-IBIG Contribution - Php100.00

Saskatchewan, Alberta, and British Columbia. ● You will also have to shoulder the following: ○ PhilHealth Insurance Premium - Php2,400.00 (Valid for 1 Year) ○ Pag-IBIG Contribution - Php100.00 per month ● You have to pay for the cost to obtain your passport, NBI and/or Police Clearance, medical, trade test, and other required documents, but you can ask the help of the recruitment agency to obtain these for you. They should charge you only the actual cost of the documents. ● No! You don't have to pay for your round-trip airfare; your employer pays for it!

2. POEA and OWWA Fee, and Insurance Coverage

Meanwhile, the employer or recruitment agency shall pay the following fees - ● POEA Processing Fee - Php200.00 ● OWWA Membership Contribution - USD25.00

This is VALID FOR 2 YEARS/ or on a Per Contract Basis

For the list of benefits under the OWWA, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG, visit: ● www.owwa.gov.ph ● www.philhealth.gov.ph ● www.pagibig.gov.ph

3. Compulsory Insurance Coverage

To prepare for any eventuality affecting the health of overseas Filipino workers, the government mandates insurance coverage for them. Each migrant worker to be deployed by a licensed recruitment agency shall be covered by a compulsory insurance contract that shall be secured and at no cost to the said worker.

The insurance shall cover the following contingencies. Accidental Death: USD15,000.00 - This type of coverage refers to the death of a worker on the way to or from the work area, on the job or off the job but within the jurisdiction of the worksite. Natural Death: USD10,000.00 - This type of coverage refers to the death of a worker due to natural causes such as heart attack, heat stroke, and the like.

Get The Prices Right: Insurance Coverage

Get The Prices Right: Insurance Coverage

Permanent or Total Disablement: USD7,500.00 - This type of coverage ensures workers' benefit for loss of limbs, eye sight, and the like.

Repatriation Cost - This type of coverage assures the worker free repatriation back to the Philippines due to natural or manmade disasters in the country of deployment.

Subsistence Allowance - USD100.00/month for 6 months - The employer and/or the recruitment agency is required to give the worker one hundred United States Dollars (US$100.00) per month for a maximum of six (6) months for a migrant worker who is involved in a case or litigation for the protection of his/her rights in the receiving country.

Compassionate Visit - In cases where the worker needs to be hospitalized for 7 or more consecutive days, the insurance company shall pay for the transportation cost of one (1) family member or requested individual to the major airport closest to the place of hospitalization of the worker.

Medical Evacuation - When an adequate medical facility is not available proximate to the migrant worker, as determined by the insurance company's physician and the consulting physician, evacuation under appropriate medical supervision by the mode of transport necessary shall be undertaken by the insurance provider.
Medical Repatriation - When medically necessary as determined by the insurance company physician and the consulting physician, repatriation under medical supervision to the migrant worker's residence

shall be undertaken by the insurance provider at such time that the migrant worker is medically cleared for travel by commercial carrier.

MODULE 5: SEAL THE DEAL

Seal The Deal: The Employment Contract

After being pre-selected for the job and knowing the fees to pay, you are just about ready to get a copy of the Employment Contract. Study its contents.

Since you will bind yourself to a legal and enforceable contract in the Philippines and the host country, go over the list of the minimum provisions. Read each one carefully. Seek the assistance of the POEA if you have any concern.

Seal The Deal: Minimum Provisions of an Employment Contract

Seal The Deal: Minimum Provisions of an Employment Contract

Place of Assignment or Specific Worksite - The building, street, city/district, and province of your worksite must be clearly stated. This should not be changed upon your arrival in the host country.

Length of the Contract - You are hired for a specific time period; this starts from the date you leave the Philippines and the date you will return. Extending your stay does not mean an automatic adjustment in your salary.

Position or Designation - This is very crucial. Make sure your designation is clearly stated. There are salary rates for specific position or job designation. Make sure you perform the tasks specified in the contracted position.

Work Schedule of 8 hours per day and 6 days a week - As overseas worker, you are required to render 8 hours of work per day, 5 or 6 days a week. Number of rest day/s must be clearly stated in the contract.

Basic Monthly Salary - This is the amount you will receive for the working hours rendered. The amount should - Your employer may assist you in remitting a percentage of your salary through the proper banking channel or other means authorized by law.

Overtime Pay Rate

- This is the pay you will receive for the work you will be asked to perform over and above the regular 8 hours. Make sure you are familiar with how this is computed.

Free transportation to & from worksite -

Your employer must provide you with free transportation going to and returning from the worksite. If the employer will not provide this, make sure there is an equivalent amount to cover for transportation expenses or there are other benefits to compensate.

Free food and accommodation - Your employer must provide you with free food and accommodation while in the worksite. If the employer will not provide this, make sure there is an equivalent amount to cover for food and accommodation expenses or there are other benefits to compensate.

Vacation leave, sick leave, medical & dental benefits - You are entitled to vacation leave and sick leave. Know the number of sick and vacation leaves available to you for the duration of your contract. Your free annual medical and dental examinations must also be included in the contract.

Seal The Deal: The Employment Contract

Compensation in case of work-related disablement or injury - Although the compulsory insurance coverage provides compensation for work-related disablement or injury, make sure this is one of the provisions included in your Employment Contract. The amount of compensation must be clearly stated.

Repatriation of remains and personal belongings - The repatriation of remains and personal belongings is the responsibility of the employer. In case repatriation is not possible, arrangements with regard to the remains will be made with the Philippine Embassy/Consulate and/or the next of kin.

Seal The Deal: Termination of Contract

In as much as your employer has a list of obligations to fulfill to ensure your productive engagement in the worksite, there are also a number of causes that your services may be terminated.

These include ● serious misconduct ● willful disobedience of employer' s lawful orders ● habitual neglect of duties ● absenteeism ● insubordination ● revealing secrets of establishment

● violation of customs, traditions, and laws of the host country and/ or terms of the Employment Contract In this situation, you will shoulder your repatriation expenses.

You too can terminate your own contract when the employer is at fault. These causes include the following: ● serious insult be the employer or his representative ● inhumane and unbearable treatment accorded the employee by the employer or his representative ● commission of a crime/offense by the employer or his representative ● violation of the terms and conditions of the employment contract by the employer or his representative In any of these cases, your employer shall shoulder your repatriation expenses.

You may also terminate the contract without just cause by serving one (1) month in advance written notice to the employer. If you fail to serve the one month notice, your employer may hold you liable for damages and you will pay for your repatriation expenses.

In case you get ill or injured, you or your employer may terminate the contract. In this regard, your employer pays for the repatriation expenses.

Seal The Deal: Contract Signing

Take a deep breath, then sign the Employment Contract!

This signed contract will be processed at the POEA and will be returned to you together with the following: ● Overseas Employment Certificate (OEC) ● Pre-Departure Orientation Seminar (PDOS) Certificate ● Passport ● Visa
One last reminder, do not agree to have these documents given to you only at the airport.
